To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel combination of adenovirus seropositive 5 (Ad 5) vectors, each targeting a distinct human tumor antigen (CEA, MUC1, brachyury) has been developed and shown in vitro to activate T cells from cancer patients, and in vivo to elicit antigen-specific CD4 and CD8 T cell responses in mice.

we have developed novel recombinant adenocarcinoma virus vaccines targeting three tumor-associated antigens and have shown that these vaccines are capable of activating antigen specific human T cells in in vitro studies and inducing antigen-specific immune responses in vaccinated mice.
we have developed a novel combination of three adenovirus seropositive 5 (AdS) vector vaccines targeting three tumor-associated antigens as an immune therapeutic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of novel recombinants of adenovirus vectors, which are capable of inducing immune responses to a wide range of tumor-associated antigents.
the design of recombinant vaccines to treat patients with advanced cancers.
the development and preclinical evaluation of novel recombinants of Ad5 [ E1-, E2B-]-based vaccine vectors that are designed to induce immune responses in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Tri-Ad5 combination of Ad5 [e1-,-e2b-]-ceas, Ad5 [e-1,-e2b]-brachy, and Ad5 [e,-e2b] -Muc1 is capable of inducing immune responses to three different TAAs, and that the Tri- Ad5 combination of Ad vaccines is capable of inducing T cell responses to multiple TAAs without antigen competition in vitro and in vivo.

the generation of a novel combination vaccine, Tri-Ad5, consisting of three adenovirus vaccines, each targeting a unique tumor-associated antigen, has been developed and shown to be safe, well-tolerated, and immunogenic in preclinical studies.

the combination of three recombinant adenoviurses targeting three TAAs, CEA, brachyury, and MUC1, is a novel combination of vaccines that is capable of eliciting immune responses to each of the TAAs in vitro, and is capable of inducing immune responses in murine vaccination models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have generated a combination vaccine targeting three different TAAs, each capable of inducing antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses in vivo, and that the combination of the three vaccine constructs does not result in “antigenic interference.”
the combination vaccine is safe in animal studies and is able to induce immune responses in vivo to multiple tumor associated antigens in a non-competitive manner.

the Tri-Ad5 vaccine is a novel combination of three recombinant Adenovirus vaccines targeting diverse tumor-associated antigens, which has been shown to activate antigen-specific human T-cells in vitro and induce antigen-specific CD4 and CD8 T-cells in vaccinated mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel combination of adenovirus vaccines that target three diverse TAAs and have demonstrated that there is minimal “antigenic” competition between the vaccines.
a novel combination of adenovirus vaccines that target three different TAAs, each expressed by a wide range of cancers, is capable of inducing immune responses to each antigen.
the use of a novel combination vaccine targeting three diverse TAAs can induce antigen-specific T-cell responses without significant “antigenic interference.”
